Cc: procurements@greenstonecap.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: disposal proof + geozone attestation for SOC2 review

Hi Evelyn —

We’re preparing for an internal SOC 2 readiness checkpoint and need a concise package showing how Redwood handles tenant record disposition across geozones. Specifically: 

- A mapping that shows TTLs/retention windows per tenant type and geozone (primary + backups).
- A sample deletion log that demonstrates the traceability chain (who/when/what was deleted).
- A brief attestation we can include in our vendor risk file stating that customer data is not retained outside declared geozones beyond retention windows.

Can you provide these artifacts or point me to a canonical packet? We’re on a tight timeline — would appreciate a response by Mon 11/23.

Thanks,
Leah Morrison
Senior Security Analyst
GreenStone Capital

Leah / team —

Quick answers from Data Lifecycle: 
- Primary + replica deletions are included in our standard deletion choreography and are observable in the deletion log. Cold snapshots (archival backups) follow a separate retention TTL (default 90 days) and are subject to the same geozone residency rules; we can include snapshot deletion markers if you require them.
- We recommend a 3-month sample window for SOC evidence (balances workload vs. signal). If you need full 12-month sampling, we can produce that but it’s larger and will take more time to scrub PII.

Notes on artifacts attached: 
- redwood-retention-mapping-20261118.csv: shows tenant class (dev/staging/prod), TTL primary, replica, snapshot TTL, and geozone tag.
- sample-deletion-log-20261031.pdf: redact columns that would identify tenant PII; retains tenant ID hash, operation, timestamp, and operator id.

I’ve also included a short guidance doc internally on how deletion events flow through our pipeline (will link in Drive).

Karthik
Senior Engineering Manager, Data Lifecycle
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we finalize the package: 

- Please include snapshot (archive) deletion markers; our auditor expects a backup retention column.
- For the attestation text, we need an explicit sentence confirming that customer data will not be replicated to regions outside declared geozones and that deletion actions remove both primary and replica records within the stated TTLs.
- For sampling, 3 months is fine. Please provide the sample run dates and a short note confirming redaction approach.

Procurements also asked whether we can get a notarized attestation or an authorized signatory name for our vendor file. If Redwood can provide an authorized signatory, we’ll add that to the vendor record and that should be sufficient (DocuSign preferred).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

-Leah
